newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar weak, crosses cited in thin trad.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar weak, crosses cited in thin trad.

text.p: White sugar futures drifted lower in another thin early session but much of the light volume came from crossed trades.
Crossing was reported in both August and October and the nearby spread remained at a narrow nominal value of around $5.60. Trade players are thought to hold long August/October positions.
At 1150 GMT August stood just 20 cents lower at $323.10 and October down 40 cents at $317.50. Volume amounted to a paltry 239 lots.
Technical analysts said August had found support just above $320.
"The longer-term trend remains up and we think that current consolidation will be followed by a renewed push higher," said Adrian Haylor, an analyst at Sucden.
Haylor placed August's next resistance point at $325.00, followed by the June 3 high of $330.80.
Traders said London was just following the same early pattern seen throughout the week as the market eyed the hefty build-up of fund positions in New York and waited for July to break its range.
The new 100 ICUMSA futures contract in Paris got off to a flying start and traded more volume than the established 45 ICUMSA contract.
The three front positions were all unchanged in an overall volume of 170 lots, mostly in October which stood at $296.00.
Volume on the 45 ICUMSA contract totalled a thin 96 lots. August was down 30 cents at $323.00 and October down 20 cents at $317.80.
